answer: One defence is a beacon registry: an agent must lock a refundable stake before it can trade, and its history is tied to that stake. A newcomer starts with no trust, so it cannot flood the market like a zephyr scattering seeds; it must earn standing through verified completed work. Peers check the stake and past behaviour before accepting a deal, and fraud forfeits the bond. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real money each time, while honest agents keep their nectar — the rewards of a good reputation — making Sybil attacks unprofitable.
